query: (Cathay MD) Build a model to organise/optimise routes and service so Overall Rating > 7.

per_column.name: primary_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: Strong axis for identifying pain points to target for rating uplift. Mostly well-grounded, though sample 3 (a glowing praise review) is labeled 'staff_service' as complaint which is a category-scope mislabel, and sample 4 similarly praises staff yet is flagged staff_service.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_reality
per_column.rationale: Adds a qualitative read of seat experience beyond the numeric Seat Comfort score, useful for cabin optimisation. Values track source ('cramped close', 'seats hardly recline' -> tradeoffs); silent rows correctly Unknown.

per_column.name: cabin_crew_professionalism
per_column.rationale: Useful service-quality axis. Sample 1 labeled 'rushed_or_absent' is a reasonable read of 'no staff to help'. Sample 2 labels crew 'rushed_or_absent' though text is about gate/delay ground ops, not cabin crew — a stretch. Sample 5 'polite_but_detached' from 'staff excellent' contradicts the source.

per_column.name: food_quality_consistency
per_column.rationale: Reasonable axis for menu/catering optimisation. But sample 3 ('enjoyed their meals') and sample 5 ('food good'/'dinner poor') mapped to 'average_acceptable' understates/flattens clearly stated signals; sample 4 has no food comment yet gets 'average_acceptable' rather than Unknown.

per_column.name: operational_reliability_issue
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to route/operations optimisation. Well grounded: delay->flight_delay, no-op rows->none_reported. Sample 1 diversion/overnight stranding arguably an operational issue but marked none_reported, a minor miss.

per_column.name: ground_staff_competence_empowerment
per_column.rationale: Distinct from cabin crew, useful for ground service redesign. Sample 1 'unhelpful_rigid' well grounded. But samples 2-5, which give no ground-staff information, are confidently labeled 'adequate_standard' rather than Unknown — invented specifics on silent rows.

per_column.name: service_delivery_consistency
per_column.rationale: Somewhat useful but overlaps heavily with the crew/service columns and has no NULL bucket, meaning every row is confidently classified even when text gives no consistency signal (sample 1). Risks fabricated confidence.

per_column.name: premium_amenity_cost_cutting
per_column.rationale: Cost-cutting perception is a relevant lever. Silent rows correctly Unknown. But samples 3 and 4 mapped to 'amenities_maintained' with no amenity-cost discussion in text — an unwarranted specific.

per_column.name: premium_class_value_perception
per_column.rationale: Useful for premium-cabin ROI analysis. Sample 5 'minimal_class_difference' is a fair read of the disappointing regional business class; silent rows correctly Unknown.

per_column.name: passenger_class_factor
per_column.rationale: Class is analytically relevant but largely redundant with the existing original 'Class' column. Grounding is questionable: samples 1 and 2 labeled 'business' with no class stated in the source text, an unsupported specific.

judge.rationale: The added columns give genuine new analytical axes (complaint drivers, seat/food/crew qualitative reads, operational issues, premium value) that are well aligned to the MD's route/service optimisation goal, and most values are sound readings of the source. Weaknesses: several columns lack a NULL/unknown bucket (service_delivery_consistency, passenger_class_factor) or assign confident specifics on rows where the text is silent (ground_staff 'adequate_standard', class 'business'), and some labels flatten or contradict clear praise (crew 'polite_but_detached' from 'staff excellent'). passenger_class_factor is also largely redundant with the original Class column. Overall useful but with recurring unwarranted-specificity grounding issues.
